summary: Share GitHub observer polls across repository aliases, preserve inclusive conditional listing boundaries with bounded reconciliation backoff, and distinguish conditional hits in admission diagnostics and telemetry.

replay.detail: No graph replay, declaration migration or stored-state backfill. Existing watches keep their subjects, deadlines and recipients. Older observer cursors default optional overlap and sweep state and safely replay their first inclusive overlap.

schema.detail: Storage version unchanged. No database or wire schema migration. Alias identity uses existing repository_id facts; optional cursor fields preserve old records. The strict local reservation ledger retains exactly its original at/caller/resource/observer/count shape. Bounded endpoint/response attribution is stored in a separate diagnostic sidecar.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule or coordinated upgrade requirement. Shared-token admission remains local to each daemon.

compatibility.detail: Standing observers for the same known repository ID elect one poll across the fleet declaration union and fan out to alias subscriptions. Unknown IDs still require discovery reads; custom non-standing observers remain independent. Item and comment requests overlap the stored watermark by one second and deduplicate by identity, update time and content digest, including repeated same-second edits. Paginated sweeps preserve exact continuations and freeze the starting watermark until two complete ordered page-version sequences agree. After two nonmatching completed sweeps, continuation falls back to ordinary observer cadence while retaining scan state and frozen watermarks; unstable sweeps are never force-committed. Idle URLs remain stable for ETag revalidation. Doctor adds bounded endpoint/status counts from a separate sidecar, distinguishing 304 hits from possible quota-bearing requests. The st.github.responses counter splits charged (completed non-304) and not_modified responses by repository and rate-limit resource, with the daemon host attribute. Conditional 304s still consume conservative local admission reservations. Admission safety depends only on the original ledger; attribution read/write failures expose a gap without blocking HTTP. Watch cadence and stopped-seat lifecycle are unchanged by this change.

downtime.detail: No additional downtime, special rollout sequence, daemon restart or live-state mutation is performed by this source change.

manual.detail: No configuration change, migration or backfill required. Compare response rates rather than durable reservations with provider quota observations. Fleet owner election and rate-limit-header backoff remain design-only options in docs/st3/github-observer-admission.md.

recovery.detail: Rollback resumes independent alias polling without removing or rewriting watches and requires no storage migration or reservation deletion. Older readers ignore optional cursor fields and never read the attribution sidecar. Reservation bytes retain exactly the old strict schema, so older enforced-cap binaries preserve spent usage and continue admitting safely. Requests without sidecar records are unknown attribution after upgrading again.
